scope: Primary sources for droplet deposition, collector efficiency and animal vapour uptake; rain, humidity and storms are committed project products named in water.py INPUT_FILES.

sources.citation: Park, K.-C., Chhatre, S. S., Srinivasan, S., Cohen, R. E. and McKinley, G. H. (2013). Optimal design of permeable fiber network structures for fog harvesting. Langmuir 29(43), 13269-13277.
sources.access: Full text read (MIT DSpace copy) by a verification agent.
sources.use: St = 2 rho_w r^2 v0/(9 mu R) with droplet radius r and fibre radius R; deposition eta_d = St/(St + pi/2), the Langmuir-Blodgett fit for a long cylinder; Raschel mesh 1.8% measured in lab fog, coated meshes 4.6-10.2%, optimum about 12%.
sources.limit: Laboratory fog, 2 m/s, droplet radius about 3 um.

sources.citation: Rivera, J. de D. (2011). Aerodynamic collection efficiency of fog water collectors. Atmospheric Research 102(3), 335-342.
sources.access: Full text of the in-press version (FogQuest) read by a verification agent.
sources.use: Overall efficiency is aerodynamic x capture x drainage; aerodynamic efficiency at most about 20-24.5%; total unlikely to exceed about 30%; about 20% measured overall in the field (Schemenauer and Joe 1989).

sources.citation: O'Donnell, M. J. (1977). Site of water vapor absorption in the desert cockroach, Arenivaga investigata. PNAS 74(4), 1757-1760.
sources.use: Gains weight from air above 82.5% RH through two bladder-like extensions of the hypopharynx.

sources.citation: Knülle, W. (1966). Journal of Medical Entomology 2(4), 335-338 (title not recorded here).
sources.use: Larvae of Dermacentor andersoni, D. variabilis and Amblyomma cajennense hold equilibrium weight down to about 80-85% RH.
sources.limit: Ticks; a precedent for vapour uptake, not an aerophyte mechanism.
